sections.h2: Where is Rogers, Arkansas, and why has it grown so fast?
sections.html:
Rogers is a city in Benton County in the Ozarks, and it is part of the Northwest Arkansas metro area. It is the sixth-most populous city in Arkansas, with 69,908 people in the 2020 census and an estimate of 76,956 for 2025, a 10.1% increase.

Growth has been fast for decades: 57.3% from 1990 to 2000, 44.1% from 2000 to 2010 and 24.9% from 2010 to 2020. Benton County as a whole went from 221,339 in 2010 to 284,333 in 2020, and its 2025 estimate is 332,554. The county ranks second in population among Arkansas's 75 counties.

For a seller, a city that grew by more than 24% in each of the last three decades has houses built in very different years. The age of the house usually decides how much work a buyer expects to do.

Rogers was established and incorporated in 1881, the year the St. Louis and San Francisco Railway, known as the Frisco, arrived, and it is named for Captain Charles W. Rogers, an officer of that railroad. In 1883 the Bentonville Railroad began in Rogers and linked it to Bentonville about six miles away.

Stroud's Mercantile, founded in 1884, was the city's leading retailer into the 1960s and closed in 1993 after 109 years. Downtown streets were paved with concrete and brick in 1924, and the brick pavement remains.

The first Walmart store opened in Rogers in 1962 under Sam Walton. Walmart's headquarters is in neighboring Bentonville, and the company's air fleet is based at Rogers Municipal Airport.

sections.h2: What are the main employers and attractions in Rogers?
sections.html:
Walmart, based next door in Bentonville, shapes the Benton County economy, along with hundreds of related businesses, and agriculture, tourism and construction also matter. The county's median household income is the highest in Arkansas.

  • Daisy Outdoor Products, known for air rifles, has its headquarters and Airgun Museum in Rogers.
  • Pinnacle Hills Promenade and Frisco Station Mall are the city's two shopping malls.
  • Walmart AMP is a music venue that has hosted major acts.
  • Pinnacle Country Club hosts the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship on the LPGA tour each June, and it has done so since 2007.
  • The city has more than 23 miles of trails, and the Razorback Regional Greenway runs 36 miles across the region.

Lake Atalanta, Beaver Lake, Hobbs State Park and Pea Ridge National Military Park, about 10 miles away, sit nearby. A seller can use these specifics in a listing or in a conversation with a buyer.

sections.h2: What does the Ozark climate and setting mean for a Rogers house?
sections.html:
Rogers has a humid subtropical climate, with warm, humid summers and generally mild to cool winters, and it sits at 1,352 feet in the Ozark hills. Hills mean sloped lots, retaining walls and drainage work, so a seller should expect buyers to look at grading and the foundation as well as the roof.

Much of eastern Benton County borders Beaver Lake, a reservoir on the White River, and most of the county's water area is in the lake. Rogers itself has Lake Atalanta and one other lake within the city.

Neighboring places also compete for the same buyers. Benton County has many incorporated municipalities, including Bentonville, Lowell, Cave Springs, Bethel Heights, Little Flock and Pea Ridge, and Springdale lies mostly across the line in Washington County. A buyer comparing Rogers with those places will notice differences in school district and tax bills, so a seller should be ready with clear answers.

The Rogers School District serves most of the city, and parts of western Rogers are in the Bentonville School District. Because the district line splits the city, sellers should confirm which district an address belongs to.

  • Rogers High School was founded in 1922 and has about 2,000 students in Class 7A.
  • Rogers Heritage High School opened in 2008 with about 2,000 students.
  • Rogers New Technology High School opened in 2013 as part of the New Tech Network.
  • Arkansas Arts Academy High School is a public charter school.
  • St. Vincent de Paul is the largest private school in the city.

Harding University, John Brown University, Bryan College and the University of Phoenix have campuses in Rogers. The University of Arkansas in Fayetteville and Northwest Arkansas Community College in Bentonville are close by.

sections.h2: How do people get around Rogers?
sections.html:
Commercial flights use Northwest Arkansas National Airport in Highfill, about 15 miles west of Rogers, while Rogers Municipal Airport (Carter Field) serves Walmart's fleet. Ozark Regional Transit provides fixed-route and dial-a-ride service. The nearest intercity bus service is Jefferson Lines in Fayetteville.

The airport distance matters to out-of-state owners and to heirs who live elsewhere, because it makes a quick trip to deal with a house practical.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules affect a Rogers house sale?
sections.html:
The City of Rogers Community Development Department handles planning and building matters from 301 W. Chestnut St., open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The main line is 479-621-1117, and the Risk Reduction Division, which handles building permits and inspections, is at 479-621-1100.

The city says a building permit is required for an accessory building that is over 10 feet tall, over 200 square feet, permanently affixed to the ground or connected to utilities. Retaining walls over 4 feet and fences over 7 feet or with concrete footings also need one. No fence permit is needed unless those conditions apply.

If a prior owner added a shed, a garage conversion or a retaining wall, ask whether a permit was pulled. Unpermitted work can become a question during a financed sale. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, but you should still tell the buyer what you know.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and closing costs work for Rogers sellers?
sections.html:
Benton County, not the city, bills the property tax. The Benton County Collector's main branch is at 215 E. Central Ave., Room 101, in Bentonville, and the phone number is 479-271-1040. Online eCheck payments are credited within 2 business days, and credit or debit card payments go through the county's separate payment page.

The state sets the rules on valuation. Properties are reappraised every 3, 4 or 5 years, and a hearing with the County Board of Equalization must be scheduled by the third Monday in August. The homestead credit is up to $500 a year, rising to up to $600 beginning with 2026 tax bills.

When the deed is recorded, Arkansas charges a transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, paid by buying a stamp. The Arkansas Real Estate Commission says sellers are not required by law to disclose everything they know, but a Seller Property Disclosure form from the Arkansas Realtors Association is widely encouraged.

faqs.q: How many people live in Rogers, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 69,908 people, and the 2025 estimate is 76,956. Rogers is the sixth-most populous city in Arkansas.

faqs.q: Which county bills property tax in Rogers?
faqs.a: Benton County does. Pay at the Benton County Collector, 215 E. Central Ave., Room 101 in Bentonville, or online through the county's payment pages.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to build a shed in Rogers?
faqs.a: It depends on the size. The city requires a building permit for accessory buildings over 10 feet tall or over 200 square feet, or ones fixed to the ground or connected to utilities.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport in Highfill, about 15 miles west, handles commercial flights. Rogers Municipal Airport serves Walmart's fleet.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Rogers house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is to a cash buyer, although you should still share the problems you know about. Arkansas has no mandatory seller disclosure statute for every sale.
